header: The shared catalog's house prep recipes, checked against sources (after
20261018000000). Stage 4C of the bottle catalog plan:
* 95 of the 103 catalog preps that carry amounts, each re-checked on the
pages it now cites: one item_sources row per fact (recipe, yield, keeps),
two sites for the staples. Where a page gave different amounts, the
recipe now follows it, and the method steps, description and keep go
with it (each entry's "fix" in the seed says what changed and why).
* A keep is the shortest any cited page gives for that recipe, or a less
preserved one. With no page to cite, the keep is cleared rather than
* Left as they are, with nothing found to cite: Rosemary syrup, Earl Grey
syrup, Grapefruit sherbet, Passionfruit cordial, Coconut cream mix,
Salt air, Citrus foam, and Tonic syrup (its quinine can't be
shown to stay under the US 83 ppm or FSANZ 100 mg/kg limits).
* An independent second check of 100 random facts (amounts, yields,
keeps) against the cited pages found 1 wrong (1%): a peel weight the
page never gave. It is fixed (no weight, the count instead).

ingredients.name: Clove oil
ingredients.description: Food-grade clove bud oil, used a drop at a time to give clove flavour without the grit of ground clove. Very strong: never more than a drop or two per batch.

preps.name: Acid-adjusted orange juice
preps.description: Fresh orange juice with citric and malic acid added to bring it up to the sourness of lime juice. Lets orange stand in for lime in a sour.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. Keep 48 h unchanged (source: 2 to 3 days for fresh orange juice).

steps.body: Juice the oranges and fine strain the juice.
Weigh the acids accurately and add them to the juice.
Stir or shake until the powders have fully dissolved.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Best on the day it is made.

sources.note: Orange to lime acidity: 3.2 g citric and 2 g malic per 100 ml juice; scaled to 1 litre.
Same chart per litre of juice: orange to lime, 32 g citric and 20 g malic.
Keep for plain fresh orange juice, less acidic than ours: 2 to 3 days in the fridge; we take the shorter end.

preps.name: Agave syrup
preps.description: Agave nectar cut with half its weight of water so it pours and balances like simple syrup. The usual sweetener in a Tommy's Margarita.
preps.fix: Line Agave syrup (this prep itself) to Agave nectar, and 1000 ml to 1000 g: Punch gives 2 parts nectar to 1 part water by weight. Imbibe runs thinner, 1:1 by volume; we use Punch. Keep 672 to 336 h: Imbibe says up to 2 weeks.

steps.body: Weigh the agave nectar and warm water into a container.
Stir or shake until evenly mixed.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 2 parts agave nectar to 1 part water by weight gives close to 50 Brix, so it balances like simple. Scaled to 1 kg nectar. We use this ratio.
Second source runs 1 cup agave to 1 cup water (1:1 by volume), a thinner syrup; we use 2:1 by weight from Punch.
Refrigerated, up to 2 weeks.

preps.name: Bacon fat-infused bourbon
preps.description: Bourbon infused with warm rendered bacon fat, then frozen and strained. Smoky and savoury; the base of the Benton's Old Fashioned.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (Punch/PDT: 1.5 oz bacon fat per 750 ml, about 42 per 700 ml; our 40 g is within 10%). Added the 4-hour infusion and 2-hour freeze. Keep cut from 2160 h to 168 h: Drinks World gives 1 to 2 weeks for fat washes.

recipe.note: rendered from smoked bacon, strained, warm and liquid

steps.body: Cook smoked bacon and strain the rendered fat. Weigh out the warm, liquid fat.
Combine the fat and bourbon in a wide container, stir, and leave at room temperature for 4 hours.
Freeze for about 2 hours, until the fat has set solid.
Remove the fat and strain the cold bourbon through a coffee filter. Bottle, label as containing pork, date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Punch (PDT): 1.5 oz (45 ml) bacon fat to 750 ml bourbon, infuse 4 hours, freeze 2 hours, strain. Scaled to 700 ml about 42; our 40 g is within 10%.
General fat-washing guide: fat-washed spirits, kept in the fridge, last about 1 to 2 weeks. We take the shorter end.

preps.name: Banana syrup
preps.description: Ripe banana macerated in sugar, warmed with a little water and rested overnight before straining. Gives natural banana flavour to daiquiris, Old Fashioneds and tiki drinks.
preps.fix: Water 300 ml to 150 ml and a pinch of salt added (source: banana, sugar and water 2 : 2 : 1 by weight); method now macerates the banana in sugar first, warms it gently, then rests it overnight in the fridge, as the source does; yield 550 ml to 400 ml (derived); keep 168 h unchanged (cited).

steps.body: Toss the cut banana in the sugar until coated and leave it to draw out its juice.
Add the water and salt and warm gently, without boiling, for about 5 minutes.
Cool, cover and rest in the fridge overnight.
Strain through a fine sieve and let it drip. Do not press the fruit, which makes the syrup cloudy and starchy.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 1 ripe banana (about 3 oz), 3 oz cane sugar, 1.5 oz water, pinch of salt: 2 : 2 : 1. Macerate 3 hours, warm 5 minutes, rest overnight, strain. Scaled to 300 g banana: 300 g sugar, 150 ml water.
Keep for this same recipe: fridge, at least three weeks.
Keep for a less sweet cooked banana syrup (133 g sugar to a third of a cup of water): fridge, up to a week. Shorter keep, so we use it.

preps.name: Banana-infused rum
preps.description: Aged rum infused with mashed ripe banana for two days and filtered. Gives natural banana flavour to daiquiris, Old Fashioneds and tiki drinks.
preps.fix: Changed from 250 g sliced banana per 700 ml for 24 hours to 3 very ripe bananas, mashed, per 750 ml rum for 48 hours in the fridge (Cuban Cocktails via Imbibe, which uses 151 demerara rum; ratio applied to aged rum). Keep removed: no source (the source's 'indefinitely' is for 151-proof rum).

steps.body: Mash the bananas in a bowl or jar and stir in the rum. Cover.
Chill in the fridge for 48 hours.
Fine strain, then pass through a coffee filter (slow: change the filter if it clogs).
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Cuban Cocktails (via Imbibe): 3 very ripe bananas, mashed, with a 750 ml bottle of demerara 151 rum, 48 hours in the fridge, then fine strained.

preps.name: Basil syrup
preps.description: Fresh basil leaves steeped in just-boiled simple syrup and strained. Sweet and peppery; used in Gin Basil Smash style drinks and daiquiris.
preps.fix: Was 50 g blanched basil blended into 500 ml simple syrup, which no basil source we reached gives. Now Tim Cooper's steeped syrup: 500 g sugar, 600 ml boiling water, 15 leaves for 30 minutes; Blend action dropped. Keep raised from 168 h to 336 h, as the source gives for this recipe.

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, away from light

steps.body: Pour the boiling water over the sugar and stir until dissolved.
Add the basil leaves and leave to steep.
Strain into a clean bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Tim Cooper (GoldBar): 2 cups sugar, 2 cups boiling water, 10 to 15 basil leaves, steeped 30 min. Converted (cup sugar 200 g, cup water 240 ml) and scaled x1.25; 15 leaves.
Keep for this same recipe: up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Beetroot syrup
preps.description: Fresh beetroot juice boiled with sugar. Earthy, sweet and deep purple; used with gin, mezcal and ginger.
preps.fix: Line changed from 800 g raw beetroot (juice amount unsourced) to 500 ml beetroot juice; sugar 500 g to 415 g (source's sweeter option is 1:1 juice to sugar in cups, about 240 ml to 200 g); method now brings it to the boil and rests 20 minutes, as the source does; yield 800 ml to 750 ml (derived); keep removed: no source (the source says only "a few weeks"; the 2 week keep found belongs to a sweeter cooked beet syrup).

recipe.note: fresh, from raw beetroot, fine strained

steps.body: Juice washed raw beetroot (or blend it and strain), then pass the juice through a fine sieve.
Heat the juice with the sugar, stirring until dissolved, and bring to the boil.
Take off the heat and leave to stand.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Base is 1 cup beet juice to half a cup sugar; for a sweeter syrup it gives 1:1 juice to sugar (cups). We use the 1:1: cups converted (240 ml, 200 g) and scaled to 500 ml juice, 415 g sugar.

preps.name: Bloody Mary mix
preps.description: Tomato juice seasoned with prepared horseradish, lemon, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, salt and pepper. Pour over ice with vodka or tequila.
preps.fix: Rescaled to Food Network's batch (64 oz tomato juice) per litre of juice: horseradish 20 g to 94 ml prepared, Worcestershire 45 to 62 ml, hot sauce 15 to 4 ml, celery salt 5 g replaced by 1 tsp kosher salt, pepper 3 g to 1 tsp; lemon kept at 60 ml (source 62 ml). keep removed: no source

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Combine all the ingredients in a jug or large container.
Stir well, taste and adjust the heat and seasoning.
Cover and chill in the fridge so the flavours come together.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before each use.

sources.note: 64 oz (1,920 ml) tomato juice, 3/4 cup horseradish, 1/2 cup each lemon juice and Worcestershire, 1 1/2 tsp hot sauce, 2 tsp each salt and pepper. Scaled to 1 litre of juice (x 0.52); cups at 240 ml.

preps.name: Brew coffee concentrate
preps.description: Coarsely ground coffee steeped in cold water at 1:5 by weight for 16 to 24 hours in the fridge, then filtered. Smooth and low in bitterness; used in coffee cocktails or diluted to drink.
preps.fix: Coffee 250 to 200 g per litre of water: 1:5 by weight is the strong concentrate the source gives (1:4 isn't sourced); steep set to 16 to 24 hours in the fridge as sourced. Keep unchanged.

steps.body: Put the ground coffee in a clean container, add the cold water and stir so all the grounds are wet.
Cover and steep in the fridge for 16 to 24 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve, then through a paper coffee filter.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Strong concentrate at 100 g coffee to 500 g water (1:5), extra coarse grind, 16 to 24 hours in the fridge. Scaled to 1 litre of water.
Keep given for strained cold brew made this way: about 1 to 2 weeks in the fridge; we use the shorter end.

preps.name: Brown butter-washed bourbon
preps.description: Bourbon mixed with nutty browned butter, frozen and strained clear. Adds toasted, caramel and biscuit notes to Old Fashioneds and Manhattans.
preps.fix: Butter cut from 120 g to 106 g per 700 ml: Greenbrier Distillery browns 1/4 lb (113 g) butter per 750 ml bourbon and freezes overnight. Whisky Advocate runs richer (1 stick per 16 oz); we follow the producer. Keep cut from 2160 h to 168 h (Drinks World 1 to 2 weeks; Whisky Advocate 2 weeks; Greenbrier 1 month).

steps.body: Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and cook, swirling, until the milk solids turn golden brown and it smells nutty. Take off the heat at once.
Let the butter cool to room temperature, away from any flame, then combine it with the bourbon in a wide container and stir well.
Cover and freeze overnight, until the butter has set solid.
Strain the cold bourbon through cheesecloth and then a coffee filter. Bottle, date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Greenbrier Distillery: brown 1/4 lb (113 g) butter, combine with a 750 ml bottle of bourbon, cool, freeze overnight, strain. Scaled to 700 ml: 106 g.
Second source runs richer: 1 stick of butter to 16 oz bourbon, rest 1 to 2 hours, freeze 24 hours. We use Greenbrier's ratio as the maker's own.
Keep belongs to this same Greenbrier brown butter-washed bourbon, refrigerated.
Keep belongs to Whisky Advocate's richer brown butter-washed bourbon, refrigerated.
General fat-washing guide: fat-washed spirits, kept in the fridge, last about 1 to 2 weeks. We take the shorter end.

preps.name: Brown sugar syrup
preps.description: Soft brown sugar dissolved in an equal cup of water. Rounder and more caramel flavoured than white syrup; used in coffee drinks and whiskey sours.
preps.fix: Water 1000 to 1200 ml: Imbibe gives 1 cup brown sugar to 1 cup water, about 200 g to 240 ml. Keep 504 to 336 h: Imbibe says up to 2 weeks.

steps.body: Combine the brown sugar and hot water.
Stir until fully dissolved, warming gently if needed.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 1 cup brown sugar to 1 cup water; at 200 g a cup of sugar and 240 ml a cup of water that is 1 : 1.2 by weight. Scaled to 1 kg sugar.
Refrigerated, up to 2 weeks.

preps.name: Butterfly pea gin
preps.description: Gin infused with dried butterfly pea flowers until deep blue. The colour shifts to purple and pink when citrus or tonic is added.
preps.fix: Flowers cut from 5 g to 1.25 g per 700 ml: a Danish recipe weighs 1.2 to 1.3 g per 70 cl and warns more is not better; THE DUKE gin uses 8 to 10 flowers per 0.7 l for about an hour. Added check from 1 hour and strain by about 2.5 hours (gin turns purple and tannic). Keep removed: no source.

recipe.note: dried flowers, or 8 to 10 whole flowers

steps.body: Add the dried flowers to the gin in a clean jar or the bottle, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature and check the colour from 1 hour.
Strain through a fine sieve or coffee filter once it is deep blue, and by about 2.5 hours at the latest: longer turns gin purple and tannic.
Bottle, label and store away from light, which fades the colour.

sources.note: Danish Things: 1.25 g dried butterfly pea flowers to 665 g (70 cl) of 40% gin or vodka, about 2 to 2.5 hours at room temperature; gin goes blue-purple past 2.5 hours.
THE DUKE (gin maker): 8 to 10 dried butterfly pea flowers per 0.7 l bottle, about one hour until the colour is right, then strain.

preps.name: Cacao-nib-infused Campari
preps.description: Campari steeped with roasted cacao nibs for three days. Adds dark chocolate depth to Negronis and Boulevardiers.
preps.fix: Cacao nibs up from 30 g to 40 g per 700 ml: Imbibe's Cacao Negroni infuses 2 oz nibs per litre of Campari for 72 hours, then refrigerates. Added the 72-hour time and changed storage to fridge. Keep cut from 4320 h to 504 h (3 weeks, same source). Wrote a description (there was none).

steps.body: Add the cacao nibs to the Campari in a clean jar, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature for 72 hours, shaking now and then.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Imbibe (Jaguar Moon): 2 oz (57 g) cacao nibs to 1 litre Campari, 72 hours, strained and refrigerated. Scaled to 700 ml: 40 g.
Keep belongs to this same cacao-infused Campari, refrigerated.

preps.name: Cane syrup
preps.description: Two parts raw, unbleached cane sugar to one part water by weight. A rich syrup with a faint grassy cane flavour, used in daiquiris and Ti' Punch.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged; keep removed: no source

steps.body: Combine the cane sugar and water in a pan over low heat.
Stir until completely dissolved, without boiling. It stays brown rather than turning clear.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Unrefined cane sugar syrup is made at 1:1 or the richer 2:1; this is the 2:1. Scaled to 1 kg sugar.
2 parts organic cane sugar to 1 part water, heated without boiling. Agrees with Punch.

preps.name: Chai syrup
preps.description: Black tea syrup simmered with toasted whole chai spices, ginger and vanilla. Lighter in sugar than simple syrup; used in whisky, rum and coffee drinks.
preps.fix: Replaced with a sourced chai syrup (Fooby): 600 ml water, 6 black tea bags, 300 g sugar, 8 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 star anise, 1 tsp peppercorns, a quarter tsp nutmeg, 1 vanilla pod, 50 g ginger. Was 500 ml water to 500 g sugar with unsourced spice weights. Method now steeps the tea first, then simmers the spices 10 minutes in the syrup. keep removed: no source (the source's 6 months is for hot-filled sealed bottles).

steps.body: Toast the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, star anise, pepper and nutmeg in a dry pan until fragrant, then let them cool.
Boil the water, take it off the heat, add the tea bags, cover and steep. Squeeze and lift out the bags.
Add the sugar, vanilla seeds and pod, ginger and toasted spices. Bring to the boil, then simmer.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Fooby (Betty Bossi): 6 dl water, 6 black tea bags, 300 g cane sugar, 1 vanilla pod, 50 g ginger; spices 8 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 star anise, 1 tsp peppercorns, a quarter tsp nutmeg. Tea steeps 10 minutes, then simmer 10. Source batch as written.

preps.name: Chamomile syrup
preps.description: Chamomile steeped in hot sugar syrup. Soft apple and honey notes; pairs with whisky, gin, pear and lemon.
preps.fix: Sugar 500 g to 415 g (source is 1 cup water to 1 cup sugar, about 240 ml to 200 g); chamomile 10 g to 8 tsp loose tea as the source measures it; tea now steeps 20 minutes in the hot syrup as the source does; keep 504 h to 336 h (source says 2 weeks).

recipe.note: unrefined sugar in the source; white works
loose dried flowers, or 8 tea bags

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar until the sugar has dissolved.
Take off the heat and steep the chamomile in the hot syrup.
Strain through a fine sieve and let it cool.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Charles Joly via Imbibe: 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar, 4 tsp loose chamomile, steeped 20 minutes in the hot syrup. Cups converted (240 ml water, 200 g sugar) and scaled to 500 ml water: 415 g sugar, 8 tsp chamomile.
Keep for this same recipe: refrigerated, up to two weeks.

preps.name: Chamomile-infused bourbon
preps.description: Bourbon infused with dried chamomile flowers for about an hour. Adds a soft floral, apple and honey note to sours and Old Fashioneds.
preps.fix: Chamomile cut from 8 g to 7 g per 700 ml and time from 90 minutes to 1 hour: Punch gives 10 g chamomile flowers per litre of spirit for one hour at room temperature. A second Punch recipe uses 12 g tea bags per 750 ml for 90 minutes; we follow the whole-flower one. Keep removed: no source.

steps.body: Add the chamomile to the bourbon in a clean jar, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature for 1 hour, shaking now and then.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter, pressing the flowers lightly.
Bottle and label.

sources.note: Punch: 10 g chamomile flowers to 1 litre gin, one hour at room temperature (or sous vide), strained through a coffee filter. Ratio applied to bourbon, scaled to 700 ml: 7 g.
Second source runs stronger: 12 g (12 bags) chamomile tea to 750 ml gin, 90 minutes, agitated every 15 minutes. We use the 10 g per litre whole-flower ratio.

preps.name: Champagne acid
preps.description: Equal parts tartaric and lactic acid in water, about 3 percent of each, after Dave Arnold. Adds a dry, wine-like brightness to stirred and carbonated drinks.
preps.fix: Water 940 to 840 ml so the blend matches the cited 420 g water to 15 g tartaric and 15 g lactic (doubled); acids unchanged at 30 g each, now about 3.3% each. Yield 1000 to 900 g. Keep removed: no source.

steps.body: Weigh the water and both acids accurately.
Stir or shake until the powders have completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Bottle and label clearly with the name and date.

sources.note: Champagne acid adapted from Dave Arnold: 420 g room temperature water, 15 g tartaric acid powder, 15 g lactic acid powder; doubled.

preps.name: Chilli tincture
preps.description: Dried chillies steeped in strong vodka until fiercely hot. Dosed by the drop or dash to add heat to a drink without changing its flavour or balance.
preps.fix: Dried chilli cut from 40 g to 25 g per 500 ml: the British tincture of capsicum in the 1918 US Dispensatory macerates 50 g per litre (the US one percolates 100 g per litre of powder; we follow the maceration method we use). Vodka now 50% ABV so the ATK keep applies. Steep about 3 days (Imbibe). Keep 8760 h confirmed.

recipe.note: dried hot chillies such as arbol or bird's eye, roughly chopped

keeps.storage: Room temperature, dropper bottle, labelled hot

steps.body: Wearing gloves, roughly chop the dried chillies and put them in a clean jar with the vodka.
Seal and leave somewhere cool and dark for about 3 days, shaking now and then.
Taste a single drop diluted in water. Leave it longer for more heat.
Strain through a coffee filter into dropper bottles and label clearly as hot.

sources.note: 1918 US Dispensatory (public domain): British tincture of capsicum is 50 g chilli to 1000 ml of 60% alcohol by maceration; scaled to 25 g per 500 ml of 50% vodka.
Time only: Range's hot chilli tincture (fresh and dried chillies in vodka) steeps 3 days before straining.
Keep belongs to ATK aromatic bitters: botanicals in 100-proof vodka plus a little simple syrup. Ours is unsweetened at 50% ABV, so at least as preserved.

preps.name: Chilli-infused tequila
preps.description: Blanco tequila briefly infused with fresh red chillies. Gives clean, sharp heat to spicy margaritas and palomas.
preps.fix: Chillies changed from 4 bird's eye to 3 fresh red chillies at jalapeno heat (such as Fresno), or 1 if habanero-hot: Punch gives 2 or 3 jalapenos per 750 ml, or one habanero-strength pepper. Tasting now every minute (Punch), not every 5 minutes. Keep removed: no source.

recipe.note: fresh red at jalapeno heat, such as Fresno, halved lengthways; use 1 if habanero-hot

steps.body: Wearing gloves, halve the chillies and add them to the tequila in a clean jar.
Infuse at room temperature, stirring and tasting every minute. Fresh chilli infuses fast.
Strain through a fine sieve as soon as the heat is where you want it.
Bottle and label. If it is too hot, blend it back with plain tequila.

sources.note: Punch: two or three jalapenos per 750 ml of spirit, or a single habanero-strength pepper; taste every minute and strain at once. Scaled to 700 ml (2.8, rounded to 3).

preps.name: Cinnamon syrup
preps.description: Simple syrup infused with toasted, crushed cinnamon sticks. A tiki staple, used in the Zombie, Jet Pilot and Don's Mix, and in winter whiskey drinks.
preps.fix: Cinnamon was 40 g per 1 kg sugar and 1 litre water (about 25 g per litre of syrup); Punch's sourced ratio is about double, 52 g per litre of 1:1 syrup, so the base is now 1 litre simple syrup. Keep cut from 504 h to 336 h (Imbibe: 2 weeks).

steps.body: Crush the cinnamon sticks and toast them in a dry pan over medium heat.
Pour in the simple syrup and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Turn the heat right down, cover and leave to stand.
Take off the heat and let it cool.
Strain through a fine sieve, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 50 g cinnamon sticks to 32 oz (960 ml) 1:1 simple syrup, toasted then heated in the syrup; scaled to 1 litre of syrup (52 g).
Second source: 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 4 cinnamon sticks, simmered 8 to 10 minutes. It counts sticks, not grams, so we use Punch's weight.
Keep for Imbibe's 1 cup sugar to 1 cup water cinnamon syrup (no sweeter than ours): up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Cinnamon tincture
preps.description: Broken cinnamon sticks steeped in strong vodka for about a week. Dashed or sprayed over drinks for a dry, woody spice note.
preps.fix: Amounts cited and unchanged: 50 g cinnamon to 250 ml is the 1:5 of the 1918 US Dispensatory tincture of cinnamon (200 g per 1000 ml). Steep changed from 5 days to about 1 week (Imbibe). Vodka now 50% ABV so the ATK keep applies. Keep 8760 h confirmed.

keeps.storage: Room temperature, dropper bottle, away from light

steps.body: Break up the cinnamon sticks and put them in a clean jar with the vodka.
Seal and leave at room temperature for about a week, shaking daily. Taste from day 3 and strain once it is strong enough.
Strain through a coffee filter into dropper or atomiser bottles and label.

sources.note: 1918 US Dispensatory (public domain): tincture of cinnamon is 200 g cinnamon to make 1000 ml (1:5). Our 50 g to 250 ml is the same ratio, macerated rather than percolated.
Time only: Chad Walsh's cinnamon tincture (The Dutch) steeps cinnamon sticks in high-proof vodka for 1 week.
Keep belongs to ATK aromatic bitters: botanicals in 100-proof vodka plus a little simple syrup. Ours is unsweetened at 50% ABV, so at least as preserved.

preps.name: Citric acid solution
preps.description: Ten percent citric acid powder dissolved in water by weight. Adds clean, lemon-like sourness by the dash or millilitre without adding juice or cloudiness.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (sources dissolve 10 g in 100 g water, about 9%; ours is an even 10% by weight, within 10%). Keep 2160 h unchanged (source: up to a year).

steps.body: Weigh the citric acid and the water accurately (900 ml of water weighs 900 g).
Stir or shake until the powder has completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Bottle in glass and label clearly with the name, strength and date.

sources.note: Team Lyan's 10% citric solution: 10 g citric acid powder to 100 g water, whisked and bottled. Ours is 100 g to 900 g, an exact 10% by weight.
Citric acid solution (10%): 10 g citric acid to 100 g water.
Keep for VinePair's 10 g in 100 g water solution (about 9%, slightly weaker than ours): up to a year (12 x 4 weeks). We keep our shorter 90 days.

preps.name: Coconut fat-washed rum
preps.description: Rum mixed with melted coconut oil, frozen and strained so the fat is removed. Leaves a rich coconut aroma and a rounder texture.
preps.fix: Coconut oil up from 100 g to 198 g per 700 ml: ATK washes 10 oz (300 ml) rum with 3 oz (85 g) unrefined coconut oil, 12 to 24 hours, then 1 to 3 hours in the freezer. Added those times. Keep cut from 2160 h to 168 h: Drinks World gives 1 to 2 weeks for fat washes (ATK says 3 months).

steps.body: Melt the coconut oil gently (warm, not hot) and pour it into a wide container with the rum. Stir or shake well.
Leave at room temperature for 12 to 24 hours, swirling now and then.
Freeze until the oil has set solid, 1 to 3 hours.
Lift off or pierce the fat cap and strain the cold rum through a coffee filter. Bottle, date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: ATK: 3 oz (85 g) unrefined coconut oil to 10 oz (300 ml) rum, 12 to 24 hours, frozen 1 to 3 hours, strained through a coffee filter. Scaled to 700 ml rum: 198 g oil.
Keep belongs to this same ATK coconut oil-washed rum, refrigerated.
General fat-washing guide: fat-washed spirits, kept in the fridge, last about 1 to 2 weeks. We take the shorter end.

preps.name: Coconut syrup
preps.description: Full-fat coconut milk sweetened with sugar, a cup of each. Creamy and lighter than tinned cream of coconut; used in tiki drinks such as the Bahama Mama.
preps.fix: Sugar 400 to 335 g and pinch of salt removed: Punch gives 1 cup coconut milk to 1 cup sugar (about 240 ml to 200 g), no salt. Keep 168 h is inside Punch's 10 days.

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Shake the tin well, then combine the coconut milk and sugar in a pan.
Warm over medium-low heat, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved. Do not boil or the milk can split.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge. The fat sets when cold; warm the bottle briefly and shake before use.

sources.note: 1 cup full-fat coconut milk to 1 cup sugar, warmed until dissolved. At 200 g a cup of sugar, scaled to a 400 ml tin.
Airtight, in the fridge, up to 10 days.

preps.name: Coffee syrup
preps.description: Strong brewed coffee sweetened with sugar. Used in Espresso Martinis, coffee Old Fashioneds and non-alcoholic serves.
preps.fix: Sugar 500 g to 425 g per 500 ml coffee (source: 360 ml strong coffee to 10.8 oz, about 306 g, sugar); yield 800 ml to 500 ml (sourced); added the source's note to brew the coffee about double strength; keep 336 h unchanged (cited).

steps.body: Brew the coffee about twice your usual strength and measure it while hot.
Stir in the sugar over a low heat until fully dissolved, then simmer a few minutes.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 12 oz (360 ml) strong brewed coffee to 10.8 oz (about 306 g) sugar, simmered 3 to 5 minutes. Scaled to 500 ml coffee: 425 g sugar.
Second source gives equal parts sugar and cold brew, unit not stated; we use the weighed ratio above.
About 360 ml from 360 ml coffee; scaled, about 500 ml.
Keep for this same recipe: airtight in the fridge, two weeks.

preps.name: Coffee-infused Campari
preps.description: Campari infused with whole roasted coffee beans for a day. Adds roast and cocoa notes to Negronis, Boulevardiers and spritzes.
preps.fix: Coffee beans up from 40 g to 53 g per 700 ml: Kevin Coe (Durham Hotel, via Imbibe) soaks 2 oz beans in a 750 ml bottle for at least 24 hours. Time changed from 'taste at 12 hours' to at least 24 hours. Keep removed: no source.

steps.body: Add the whole coffee beans to the Campari in a clean jar or the bottle and seal.
Infuse at room temperature for at least 24 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve.
Bottle and label.

sources.note: Kevin Coe, The Durham Hotel (Imbibe): 2 oz (57 g) coffee beans to a 750 ml bottle of Campari, at least 24 hours, then strained. Scaled to 700 ml: 53 g.

preps.name: Cucumber syrup
preps.description: Peeled, seeded cucumber blitzed with sugar and left to macerate cold for a day, then strained. Clean, fresh cucumber flavour for gin coolers, gimlets and sodas.
preps.fix: Replaced the juice method (no source found) with the sourced cold method: peeled, seeded cucumber blitzed with 95% of its weight in sugar, rested 24 hours in the fridge, then strained; sugar 500 g to 665 g for 700 g cucumber; keep removed: no source (the only cucumber syrup keep found is for a boiled version, which does not carry over to this uncooked one).

recipe.note: weighed after peeling, trimming and seeding

steps.body: Peel the cucumber, cut off the ends, halve it lengthways, scoop out the seeds and slice. Weigh it.
Blitz the cucumber with 95% of its weight in sugar until finely chopped, not puréed.
Seal and rest in the fridge.
Strain through a fine sieve, then through cloth. Bottle and keep in the fridge; the fresh flavour fades quickly.

sources.note: Stateline Distillery: peeled, seeded cucumber plus 95% of its weight in sugar, blitzed, rested 24 hours cold, strained. For 700 g cucumber, 665 g sugar.

preps.name: Cucumber-infused gin
preps.description: Gin infused with peeled cucumber for a day. Cool and green; used in Martinis, gin and tonics and summer coolers.
preps.fix: Changed from 300 g sliced, skin-on cucumber per 700 ml overnight to 0.7 cucumber (half per 500 ml), peeled and deseeded, for 24 hours and no longer (Great British Chefs; its optional sugar left out). Keep cut from 2160 h to 672 h: same source says best within 1 month.

recipe.note: peeled, deseeded and cut into batons (about two thirds of one)

steps.body: Peel and deseed the cucumber, cut it into batons and put them in a clean jar with the gin. Seal.
Leave somewhere cool and dark for 24 hours, no longer, or the gin turns watery.
Strain through muslin or a coffee filter, without pressing the cucumber.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Serve chilled.

sources.note: Great British Chefs: half a cucumber, peeled, deseeded and cut into batons, to 500 ml gin (50 g sugar optional), 24 hours cool and dark, strained through muslin. Scaled to 700 ml: 0.7 cucumber.
Keep belongs to this same Great British Chefs cucumber gin; its sugar is optional, so the keep covers the unsweetened version we use.

preps.name: Demerara syrup
preps.description: Equal parts demerara sugar and water by weight. Adds a light toffee and molasses note to rum, whiskey and coffee drinks.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. Keep 504 to 336 h: Imbibe says up to 2 weeks.

steps.body: Combine the demerara sugar and hot water in a pan or heatproof container.
Stir over low heat until fully dissolved. The large crystals take longer than white sugar.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Demerara is made into syrup at 1:1 or 2:1; this is the 1:1. Scaled to 1 kg sugar.
Same 1:1 proportions as simple syrup, 1 cup demerara to 1 cup water. Agrees with Punch.
Refrigerated, up to 2 weeks.

preps.name: Don's mix
preps.description: Donn Beach's blend of two parts white grapefruit juice to one part cinnamon syrup, decoded by Jeff Berry. The signature flavour of the Zombie and Donga Punch.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. keep removed: no source (sources say to combine as needed; the 1 month keep they give is for the cinnamon syrup alone).

steps.body: Juice the grapefruit and fine strain it.
Combine two parts juice with one part cinnamon syrup and stir.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

sources.note: Two parts white grapefruit juice to one part cinnamon syrup (Jeff Berry's decoding).
Same 2:1 ratio, mixed as needed.

preps.name: Don's spices No. 2
preps.description: Donn Beach's tiki spice mix from 1937: equal parts vanilla syrup and allspice dram. Used in the Nui Nui and other Don the Beachcomber drinks.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. keep removed: no source.

steps.body: Measure equal parts vanilla syrup and allspice dram into a bottle.
Shake to combine, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Equal parts vanilla-infused 1:1 simple syrup and allspice (pimento) dram.

preps.name: Earl Grey-infused gin
preps.description: Gin infused with loose Earl Grey tea for two hours. The tea adds bergamot and tannin; it is the base of the Earl Grey MarTEAni.
preps.fix: Tea up from 10 g to 16 g per 700 ml: Punch gives 4 tbsp loose Earl Grey per 750 ml for two hours, weighed at 17 g on Kindred. Added the two-hour time. Storage changed to fridge (Punch). Keep removed: no source (Punch says only 'indefinitely').

steps.body: Add the loose tea to the gin in a clean jar or the bottle, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature for 2 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter. Do not squeeze the leaves.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Punch (Audrey Saunders, Pegu Club): 4 tbsp loose Earl Grey in a 750 ml bottle of gin, two hours at room temperature, strained; stored refrigerated.
Kindred Cocktails: 4 tbsp weighed at 17 g, per 750 ml gin for 2 hours. Scaled to 700 ml: 16 g.

preps.name: Eggnog Base
preps.description: Eggs blended with sugar, milk and cream, without spirits. Add brandy, rum or bourbon per serve, or serve it plain as a non-alcoholic nog, with nutmeg grated on top.
preps.fix: Sugar 250 to 225 g to match Morgenthaler's 75 g per 2 eggs (his base recipe tripled, with the brandy and rum left out); nutmeg moved out of the batch to a grated garnish, as the source now does. Yield removed: eggs are counted by number, so a volume can't be checked. Keep unchanged.

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Blend the eggs on medium speed for a minute (a few seconds on low in a high-powered blender).
With the blender running, add the sugar slowly and blend for another minute.
Add the milk and cream and blend just until combined.
Bottle and chill thoroughly. Grate nutmeg over each serve. Contains raw egg: keep cold, use within two days and tell guests.

sources.note: 2 large eggs, 75 g superfine sugar, 6 oz whole milk and 4 oz heavy cream (plus 2 oz each brandy and spiced rum, left out here), nutmeg grated on top. Tripled; oz at 30 ml.
University of Delaware Extension, general keep for homemade eggnog: 2 to 4 days refrigerated, do not freeze. We use the shorter end.

preps.name: Elderflower cordial
preps.description: Fresh elderflower heads steeped for a few days in a strong 1:1 syrup with sliced lemon and citric acid. A floral British cordial for spritzes, gin drinks and sodas.
preps.fix: Changed to Olivia Potts's recipe (Spectator): 1.5 kg sugar, 1.5 l water, 2 lemons, 15 heads, 50 g citric acid. Sugar 1000 g to 1500 g, heads 25 to 15; steep 2 to 4 days (was untimed). Keep 672 h to 1008 h (at least six weeks, for this recipe). Yield 2000 ml to the stated 1.5 l.

recipe.note: fresh flower heads, shaken clean, thick stalks trimmed

steps.body: Warm the sugar and water in a large pan, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Bring to the boil, then turn off the heat.
Add the elderflower heads, lemon slices and citric acid. Cover and leave for 2 to 4 days, stirring once a day.
Ladle through a sieve lined with muslin and let it drip through without pressing.
Pour into sterilised bottles, seal and keep in the fridge. Freeze any extra in tubs.

sources.note: 1.5 kg caster sugar, 1.5 l water, 2 lemons sliced, 15 elderflower heads, 50 g citric acid; steep 2 to 4 days.
Stated yield 1.5 litres.
At least six weeks in the fridge, for this recipe.
Second source: 1 kg sugar to 1 l water (same 1:1), 50 g citric acid, zest of 2 lemons, 15 heads, 1 to 2 days.

preps.name: Falernum syrup
preps.description: An alcohol-free falernum: a 1:1 syrup spiced with ginger, clove, cinnamon and lime zest. Use in place of falernum liqueur in Corn 'n' Oil, Zombies and swizzles.
preps.fix: Changed to Savour Calgary's alcohol-free ratio, doubled: 750 ml water, 750 g sugar, 10 g clove, 10 g lime zest, 60 g ginger, 2 cinnamon sticks, warmed to 60 C. Removed almonds (not in that recipe), cut ginger 50 to 60 g scaled, lime zest 20 to 10 g, added cinnamon. Old steps named allspice with no allspice line. Imbibe (McCoy) has almonds and allspice but measures by the cup and spikes it with rum, so not mixed in.

steps.body: Pulse the water, cloves, lime zest, ginger and cinnamon in a blender until the spices are roughly chopped.
Tip into a pan and warm to about 60 C.
Add the sugar and stir over the heat until dissolved.
Strain while still hot through a fine sieve, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 375 ml water, 5 g cloves, 5 g lime zest, 30 g ginger, 1 cinnamon stick, 375 g sugar, heated to about 60 C and strained hot. Doubled.
Up to 2 weeks in the fridge, for this alcohol-free recipe.

Second source (Bob McCoy via Imbibe) makes a spiced syrup with almonds, ginger, clove, allspice, star anise and lime zest, about 1 quart sugar to 1 quart water, then adds rum. We use Savour Calgary's weighed, alcohol-free ratio.

preps.name: Fassionola
preps.description: A red tropical syrup from the early tiki era: passion fruit and guava with hibiscus and a little pomegranate molasses, cooked gently sous vide. Used in the Hurricane and Cobra's Fang.
preps.fix: No source has the old strawberry, raspberry and hibiscus version. Replaced with State Line Distillery's weighed recipe (passion fruit puree, guava puree, pomegranate molasses, dried hibiscus, sugar, water; sous vide 1 h at 145 F), scaled by 2.5. Strawberry and raspberry removed, guava puree and pomegranate molasses added. Keep 336 h to 504 h, the source's keep for this recipe.

steps.body: Weigh everything into a vacuum bag and seal it.
Cook sous vide at 63 C (145 F) for 1 hour.
Chill the bag in an ice bath.
Strain through cheesecloth or a coffee filter, then keep in the fridge in a sealed container.

sources.note: 120 g passion fruit puree, 46 g guava puree, 19 g pomegranate molasses, 12 g dried hibiscus, 200 g sugar, 240 g water; sous vide 1 h at 145 (F). Scaled by 2.5.
Use within 3 weeks, refrigerated, for this recipe.

preps.name: Ginger cordial
preps.description: Fresh ginger and lemon boiled down with sugar into a thin syrup, then sharpened with citric acid. A warm, spicy base for highballs and non-alcoholic serves.
preps.fix: Replaced with Olive Magazine's ratio: ginger 300 to 200 g, water 600 to 1500 ml, sugar 500 to 600 g, 100 ml lemon juice replaced by 1 whole lemon (rind and juice), 15 g citric acid added. Ginger is now boiled with the sugar for about 40 minutes to a thin syrup. Yield 900 to 2000 ml (sourced). Keep 336 h unchanged (source allows 3 months).

recipe.note: rind peeled in wide strips, plus its juice

steps.body: Put the ginger in a large pan with the lemon rind and juice, cover with the water, add the sugar and stir over a low heat until it has dissolved.
Bring to the boil and cook until the ginger is very soft and the liquid has reduced to a thin syrup. Loosen with a little boiled water if it gets too thick.
Take off the heat and stir in the citric acid.
Strain through muslin into a sterilised bottle, leave to cool, then seal, label and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 200 g root ginger, 1 lemon (rind and juice), 1.5 L water, 600 g golden caster sugar, 15 g citric acid; boil about 40 minutes to a thin syrup, add the acid off the heat, strain through muslin.
Makes about 2 litres.
Keep for this same Olive Magazine recipe: fridge, use within 3 months. We keep our shorter 2 weeks.

preps.name: Ginger syrup
preps.description: Fresh ginger juice with an equal weight of sugar, warmed only enough to dissolve it so it keeps its bite. Used in Mules, Bucks and the Penicillin; make small batches, as it keeps only a couple of days.
preps.fix: Line changed from 900 g ginger root (an unsourced juice yield) to 500 g ginger juice, so the 1:1 by weight is exact. Method now warms gently to dissolve, as both sources do. Keep cut from 336 h to 48 h (Difford: up to 2 days).

recipe.note: freshly juiced from the root, skin on, fine strained
caster, equal to the weight of the juice

steps.body: Wash the ginger (no need to peel), run it through a juicer and fine strain the juice.
Weigh the juice into a pan and add the same weight of caster sugar.
Warm very gently, stirring, just until the sugar has dissolved. Do not let it get hot.
Fine strain into a clean bottle, seal and keep in the fridge. Use within two days.

sources.note: Equal weights of fresh ginger juice and caster sugar, warmed gently to dissolve; scaled to 500 g juice. Difford notes Sam Ross's version runs 4 juice to 3 sugar.
Second source: 1 part juicer ginger juice to 1 part white sugar (plus a pinch of chilli flakes), heated to dissolve. Agrees with the 1:1.
Keep for this same recipe (equal weights juice and sugar, gently warmed): up to 2 days in the fridge.

preps.name: Gomme syrup
preps.description: Rich sugar syrup thickened with gum arabic. It gives stirred drinks and sours a smooth, silky texture and was the standard bar syrup of the 1800s.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (Imbibe 2 : 12 : 6 oz gum, sugar, water). Steps follow its 2 day soak and take the syrup off the heat once the gum goes in. Keep 1344 to 672 h: Imbibe says up to 1 month.

recipe.note: 150 ml to soak the gum, 300 ml for the syrup

steps.body: Stir the gum arabic into 150 ml of water, cover and leave until it has fully dissolved into a thick paste, up to 2 days. Stir now and then.
Warm the sugar with the remaining 300 ml of water over low heat until it starts to dissolve.
Fold in the gum mixture, take the pan off the heat straight away and skim any foam.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 12 oz sugar, 6 oz water and 2 oz gum arabic (6 : 3 : 1), a third of the water used to soak the gum. Scaled to 900 g sugar.
Refrigerated, up to 1 month.

preps.name: Grenadine
preps.description: Pomegranate juice and sugar rounded out with pomegranate molasses, a little lemon and orange flower water. Tart, red and fruity; used in the Jack Rose and Tequila Sunrise.
preps.fix: Sugar 500 g to 415 g: Cocktail Society gives 2 cups juice to 2 cups sugar (about 400 g), scaled to 500 ml juice. Added 15 ml lemon juice, which that recipe lists. Keep 672 h to 336 h (Imbibe's 2 weeks is shorter).

steps.body: Warm the pomegranate juice, sugar and pomegranate molasses over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Keep it below a boil, which browns the colour and dulls the fruit.
Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and orange flower water.
Leave to cool to room temperature, then bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 2 cups juice, 2 cups sugar, 2 oz pomegranate molasses, 1 to 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp orange flower water (optional vodka left out). Sugar at 200 g a cup; scaled to 500 ml juice.
Four weeks in the fridge for this same recipe without vodka.
Second source agrees on juice to sugar (8 oz juice to 1 cup sugar) but runs twice the molasses and no lemon; we use Cocktail Society's ratio.
Two weeks in the fridge, for Imbibe's near recipe (same juice to sugar, more molasses, no lemon). We take this shorter keep.

preps.name: Heavy Cream, Lightly Whipped
preps.description: Cold cream shaken only until it thickens but still pours. Floated over the back of a spoon onto an Irish Coffee so it sits on top.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. Yield 300 to 250 ml (no sourced gain in volume).

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed container; re-shake before use

steps.body: Pour the cold cream into a shaker tin, squeeze bottle or bowl.
Shake or whisk until it thickens to the texture of pouring yoghurt. It should ribbon off a spoon, not hold peaks.
Keep cold. Pour slowly over the back of a spoon to float it on the drink.

sources.note: 1/3 cup (80 ml) heavy cream per Irish Coffee, shaken or whisked until thicker but still fluid, then layered over the drink with a spoon. 250 ml is about three serves.
Ohio State Extension storage chart, general keep for (lightly sweetened) whipped cream: 1 day refrigerated.

preps.name: Hibiscus syrup
preps.description: Dried hibiscus flowers simmered in sugar syrup and strained. Deep red, tart and cranberry-like; used in margaritas, spritzes and sodas.
preps.fix: Hibiscus 25 g to 52 g and sugar 500 g to 520 g per 500 ml water (source: 25 g flowers, 240 ml water, 250 g sugar); method now simmers everything 10 minutes then steeps 10 minutes, as the source does; keep 504 h to 336 h (shortest sourced keep, 2 weeks).

steps.body: Put the hibiscus, sugar and water in a pan and heat gently, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to the boil, then turn down low and simmer.
Take off the heat and leave the flowers to steep.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 25 g dried hibiscus, 240 ml water, 250 g caster sugar; simmer 10 minutes, steep 10. Scaled to 500 ml water: 52 g hibiscus, 520 g sugar. A second recipe (Charming Cocktails) uses more flower, 40 g per 237 g water; we use this one.
Keep for this same recipe: fridge, about a month.
Keep for a less sweet hibiscus syrup (200 g sugar per 237 g water): around two weeks in the fridge. Shorter keep, so we use it.

preps.name: Honey syrup
preps.description: Two parts honey loosened with one part warm water by weight so it pours and mixes cold. Used in the Bee's Knees, Gold Rush and Brown Derby.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. Keep 672 to 336 h: Imbibe says up to 2 weeks. Took the 2:1 aliases from Rich honey syrup, now 3:1.

steps.body: Weigh the honey into a container and add the warm water.
Stir until the honey has fully blended into the water. Do not boil; heat drives off the honey's aroma.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Honey syrup is 2 parts honey to 1 part hot water, shaken or stirred to dissolve. Scaled to 1 kg honey.
One part warm water stirred into two parts honey. Agrees with Punch.
Its honey syrup (1 cup honey to 1 cup water, thinner than ours) keeps up to 2 weeks in the fridge; we use that.

preps.name: Honey-ginger syrup
preps.description: Honey syrup simmered and steeped with fresh ginger. The sweet and spicy base of the Penicillin.
preps.fix: Honey 700 g to 480 ml, water 500 to 480 ml, ginger 150 to 200 g: Difford's gives 100 g ginger per cup of honey and cup of water; doubled. Added its 5 minute simmer and 12 hour steep. Keep 336 to 72 h: Difford's says use within three days.

steps.body: Combine the honey, water and sliced ginger in a pan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat, cool, then cover and leave to steep in the fridge for 12 hours.
Strain out the ginger, pressing lightly, then bottle and keep in the fridge. Use within three days.

sources.note: 100 g peeled, sliced ginger with 1 cup honey and 1 cup water, simmered 5 minutes and steeped 12 hours cold. Doubled (480 ml each, 200 g ginger).
Refrigerated, use within three days.

preps.name: Horchata
preps.description: A Mexican drink of ground rice and blanched almonds soaked with cinnamon, blended, strained and sweetened. Milky and lightly spiced; used with rum and coffee.
preps.fix: Rewritten to Joshua Kimball's horchata (Imbibe, adapted from Rick Bayless): rice 200 g to 120 ml (1/2 cup) plus 360 ml blanched almonds, water 1000 ml to 1200 ml hot plus 720 ml cold, sugar 100 to 150 g, one cinnamon stick kept, vanilla dropped; batch now about 1.9 litres. Keep unchanged.

recipe.note: hot, in two parts (720 ml then 480 ml)

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Grind the rice to a powder in a spice grinder, then pulse it with the almonds in a food processor until it looks like coarse meal.
Tip into a bowl with the cinnamon stick, stir in 720 ml of hot water, cover and refrigerate for 10 hours.
Blend the mixture on high in batches for 5 minutes.
Add the sugar and the remaining 480 ml of hot water and blend again for 3 minutes.
Strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve into a jug, stir in the cold water, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 1/2 cup rice, 1 1/2 cups blanched almonds, 1 cinnamon stick, 5 cups hot water in two parts, 3/4 cup sugar, 3 cups cold water. Cups at 240 ml; 3/4 cup sugar at about 150 g.
About 8 cups (1,920 ml) for this batch.
Keep given for this same horchata: up to three days in the fridge.

preps.name: Hot buttered rum batter
preps.description: Softened butter creamed with demerara and icing sugar, vanilla ice cream, cinnamon, vanilla and a drop of clove oil. Stir a heaped spoonful into aged rum and hot water.
preps.fix: Rewritten to Marco Dionysos's batter (Imbibe), scaled to 250 g butter: brown sugar 250 g to 333 g demerara plus 3 tbsp icing sugar, adds 90 ml vanilla ice cream, a drop of clove oil replaces ground clove, ground nutmeg and salt dropped (nutmeg goes on as a garnish); serve set to the source's 60 ml rum and 150 ml hot water. Keep unchanged.

steps.body: Let the butter and ice cream soften at room temperature.
Cream the butter and ice cream with the sugars, starting with the icing sugar, then beat in the cinnamon, vanilla and clove oil until smooth.
Pack into an airtight tub and keep in the fridge, or freeze.
To serve, stir a heaped spoonful of batter into 60 ml of aged rum and 150 ml of hot water in a warm mug. Grate nutmeg over the top.

sources.note: 1 lb each dark and light demerara, 1/2 cup powdered sugar, 1 1/2 lb unsalted butter, 1 cup vanilla ice cream, 2 to 3 drops clove oil, 1 tbsp each cinnamon and vanilla. Scaled x 0.37 to 250 g butter.
Keep given for this same batter: up to a month in the fridge or 3 months frozen. We keep our shorter 2 weeks.

preps.name: House ginger beer
preps.description: Fresh ginger juice, lemon juice and simple syrup in cold water, carbonated in a soda siphon. Spicier and drier than most bottled ginger beers; for Mules.
preps.fix: Rewritten to Morgenthaler's 1 ginger juice : 2 lemon : 2 simple syrup : 11 water, scaled to 60 ml ginger juice: ginger 200 g root (about 100 ml juice) to 60 ml juice, sugar 150 g to 120 ml simple syrup, water 750 to 660 ml, lemon unchanged at 120 ml. keep removed: no source

recipe.note: freshly juiced and strained through a fine cloth

steps.body: Juice the ginger and strain it through a fine cloth so no fibre is left to block the siphon.
Stir the ginger juice, lemon juice and simple syrup into the cold water.
Chill until very cold. Cold liquid holds more gas.
Pour into a soda siphon, seal and charge with CO2, shake once and refrigerate. Never open a siphon while it is under pressure.

sources.note: One 16 oz bottle: 1 oz ginger juice, 2 oz lemon juice, 2 oz simple syrup, 11 oz water (cold for a soda siphon), charged with CO2. Scaled x 2 to 60 ml ginger juice; oz at 30 ml.

preps.name: Jalapeño syrup
preps.description: Simple syrup steeped with sliced fresh jalapeño. Adds green chilli flavour and steady heat to margaritas and palomas.
preps.fix: Sugar 500 g to 415 g and jalapeño 2 to 5 per 500 ml water (both sources: 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar, 2 to 3 jalapeños); yield 800 ml to 750 ml (sourced); keep 336 h unchanged (cited).

recipe.note: sliced, seeds left in for more heat

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved and just simmering.
Take off the heat, add the sliced jalapeño and steep. Taste after 10 minutes and strain earlier if it is hot enough.
Strain, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 2 to 3 sliced jalapeños. Cups converted (200 g sugar, 240 ml water) and scaled to 500 ml water: 415 g sugar, 5 jalapeños.
Same ratio: 2 to 3 jalapeños to 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water.
About 1.5 cups (360 ml) per 1 cup water; scaled to 500 ml water, about 750 ml.
Keep for this same recipe: covered in the fridge, up to a month.
Keep for a recipe with the same ratio: about a month cold, best within two weeks as the chilli flavour changes. We use two weeks.

preps.name: Jalapeño-infused tequila
preps.description: Blanco tequila infused for about two days with sliced jalapeño. Adds green, vegetal chilli flavour and moderate heat to margaritas.
preps.fix: Jalapeno changed from 3 whole to 47 g (about 2) per 700 ml: The Infatuation uses 50 g (two jalapenos) per 750 ml. Time changed from about 20 minutes to about 2 days, plus a day if mild, as the source gives. Keep removed: no source.

recipe.note: about 2, sliced, with seeds and ribs

steps.body: Slice the jalapeños and add them, seeds and all, to the tequila in a clean jar.
Seal and leave somewhere cool and dark for about 2 days. Heat varies a lot from one jalapeño to the next.
Taste. If it is still mild, give it another day.
Strain through a fine sieve, bottle and label.

sources.note: The Infatuation: two jalapenos (50 g) to a 750 ml bottle of blanco tequila, two days cool and dark, another day if mild. Scaled to 700 ml.

preps.name: Lactic acid solution
preps.description: Liquid lactic acid diluted in water, Team Lyan's 5 percent mix. Gives a soft, creamy, yoghurt-like sourness; used by the drop or dash to round out clarified and stirred drinks.
preps.fix: No source gives a 10% lactic solution. Replaced with Team Lyan's 5% solution: 5 g lactic acid (sold as about 70% liquid) to 100 g water, scaled to 50 g to 1000 ml (was 100 g powder to 900 ml). Yield 1000 to 1050 g. Dropped the alias 'lactic acid solution 10'. Keep removed: no source.

recipe.note: food grade liquid as sold (usually about 70%)

steps.body: Weigh the lactic acid and the water accurately. Wear gloves: concentrated acid is corrosive.
Stir until completely blended.
Bottle in glass and label clearly with the name, strength and date.

sources.note: Team Lyan's 5% lactic solution: 5 g lactic acid (usually sold as a 70% solution) to 100 g water; scaled to 1 litre of water.
The same 5 g to 100 g solution, used by the drop in White Lyan's Creamy Martini.

preps.name: Lavender syrup
preps.description: Simple syrup boiled with dried culinary lavender and steeped briefly. Floral and lightly herbal; used in gin sours, spritzes and lemonades.
preps.fix: Was 500 ml water, 500 g sugar, 8 g lavender; the source converts to 540 ml water, 450 g sugar and 6 tbsp lavender (measured by volume, as the source does), steeped 15 minutes. Keep cut from 504 h to 336 h (Imbibe: 2 weeks).

steps.body: Bring the water, sugar and lavender to the boil, stirring until the sugar has dissolved.
Take off the heat and steep. Longer steeping turns it soapy.
Strain into a clean bottle, cool and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Matthew Biancaniello: 3/4 cup sugar, 3/4 cup water, 2 tbsp culinary lavender, boiled then steeped 15 min. Converted (cup sugar 200 g, cup water 240 ml) and scaled x3.
Keep for this same recipe: up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Lemon sherbet
preps.description: Lemon oleo saccharum dissolved in an equal measure of fresh lemon juice. A sweet and sour punch base with the full aroma of the peel.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (sugar to juice about 1:1, peels of about 8 lemons per 500 ml). Keep 168 h to 336 h, the source's keep for this recipe. Peel weight removed after the audit: the source counts lemons (4 per 8 oz juice) and gives no weight.

recipe.note: the peels of the lemons you juice: about 4 lemons per 240 ml of juice

steps.body: Muddle the lemon peels with the sugar, cover and rest for several hours or overnight until the sugar is wet and oily.
Add the lemon juice and stir or shake until all the sugar has dissolved.
Strain out the peels, pressing them well.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Peels of 4 lemons and 8 oz sugar made into an oleo, then 8 oz lemon juice (based on David Wondrich's Punch). Scaled to 500 ml juice.
Around 2 weeks in the fridge, for this sherbet.

preps.name: Lemongrass syrup
preps.description: Simple syrup infused with bruised lemongrass. Citrusy and lightly gingery; pairs with gin, vodka, coconut and lime.
preps.fix: Sugar 500 g to 415 g and lemongrass 100 g to 7 stalks per 500 ml water (source: 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar, 3 to 4 stalks); simmer time added (3 to 5 minutes, sourced); yield 800 ml to 750 ml (derived); keep 336 h unchanged (cited).

recipe.note: stalks, trimmed, inner core cut in 2 to 3 cm pieces and bruised

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved.
Add the lemongrass and simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes.
Take off the heat, cover and leave to cool.
Strain through a fine sieve, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 3 to 4 lemongrass stalks; simmer 3 to 5 minutes. Cups converted (200 g, 240 ml) and scaled to 500 ml water: 415 g sugar, 7 stalks.
Keep for this same recipe: covered in the fridge, up to two weeks.

preps.name: Lime acid
preps.description: A clear solution of 4 percent citric and 2 percent malic acid that matches the sourness of lime juice. Used to acidify stirred or clarified drinks.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. Keep removed: no source.

steps.body: Weigh the water and both acids accurately.
Stir or shake until the powders have completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Bottle and label clearly with the name and date. Use measure for measure where a recipe needs the acidity of lime juice.

sources.note: Dave Arnold's lime acid as quoted: 94 g filtered water, 4 g citric acid, 2 g malic acid (a trace of succinic acid optional); scaled to 1 kg.
Lime juice is 4% citric and 2% malic acid, the strength this solution copies.

preps.name: Lime cordial
preps.description: Fresh lime juice and an equal weight of sugar steeped with lime peel for a day. A fresh house version of bottled lime cordial, used in the Gimlet.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (equal weight sugar to juice). The peel weight is ours: sources use the zest of every lime juiced. Steep set to 24 h at room temperature as the source does (was an untimed fridge steep).

recipe.note: zest of all the limes juiced, no white pith

steps.body: Peel or zest the limes thinly before juicing them, avoiding the white pith.
Weigh the juice and stir in the same weight of sugar, without heat, until it has mostly dissolved.
Add the peel, cover and leave at room temperature for 24 hours.
Strain out the peel, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Lime juice with an equal weight of sugar and the zest of the same limes, left 24 h at room temperature, then strained (adapted from Death and Co).
Two weeks in the fridge on the recipe card for this cold-steeped recipe (the post body says up to a month; we take the shorter).
Second source: lime juice plus an equal weight of sugar and the zest, warmed short of a boil and rested 2 h.
Two weeks refrigerated, for this heated version of the same ratio.

preps.name: Maple syrup mix
preps.description: Two parts pure maple syrup thinned with one part water so it measures and mixes easily in cold drinks. Used in whiskey sours and autumn cocktails.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (Modern Farmer: half a cup of maple to a quarter cup of hot water).

steps.body: Measure the maple syrup and hot water into a jar.
Close and shake until evenly mixed.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Diluted maple spoils faster than the pure syrup.

sources.note: Half a cup of maple syrup shaken with a quarter cup of hot water (2:1 by volume). Scaled to 1 litre maple.
Chilled, up to a month. We keep 2 weeks, inside that.

preps.name: Michelada mix
preps.description: Lime juice seasoned with Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce and a little Maggi or soy. Add about 65 ml to a salt-rimmed mug of ice and top with cold Mexican lager.
preps.fix: Rescaled to Rick Bayless's michelada per 250 ml lime: Worcestershire 60 to 10 ml, hot sauce 60 to 10 ml, soy or Maggi 30 to 2.5 ml; black pepper dropped (not in the source); serve changed from 30 ml to about 65 ml per beer. keep removed: no source

recipe.note: the source uses Jugo Maggi; use it if you have it

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Juice and fine strain the limes.
Combine all the ingredients and stir well. Bottle and keep in the fridge.
To serve, rub a mug rim with lime and dip it in coarse salt, half fill with ice, add about 65 ml of mix and top with beer. Stir once.

sources.note: Per beer: 1/4 cup lime juice, about 1/8 tsp Maggi, 1/2 tsp Worcestershire and 1/2 tsp hot sauce, over ice in a salt-rimmed mug. Scaled x 4.2 to 250 ml lime; 1/4 cup at 60 ml.

preps.name: Mint syrup
preps.description: Blanched mint leaves blended into cold rich syrup and strained. Bright green and fresh; used in juleps, Southsides and batched mint drinks.
preps.fix: Was 50 g mint leaves in 500 ml 1:1 simple syrup; Morgenthaler's sourced method uses 6 to 8 sprigs in 480 ml 2:1 rich syrup, so the syrup line is now Rich simple syrup and mint is 7 sprigs. Blanch, ice and blend times added. Keep 168 h unchanged (source allows 2 weeks).

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, away from light

steps.body: Hold the mint by the stems and dip it in boiling water.
Move it straight into iced water. This sets the green colour.
Pat dry, pick the leaves and blend them with the cold rich syrup.
Strain through a fine sieve, bottle and keep in the fridge. The colour and freshness fade after about a week.

sources.note: Jeffrey Morgenthaler (Bar Book): 6 to 8 mint sprigs blanched 15 s, iced 1 min, blended 1 min with 16 oz (480 ml) 2:1 rich syrup. We use 7 sprigs.
Keep for this same recipe: up to 2 weeks. We keep the shorter 1 week already in use, for colour.

preps.name: Muscovado syrup
preps.description: Dark muscovado sugar dissolved in a little more than its weight of water. Deep molasses, liquorice and dried fruit notes that suit aged rum and whisky drinks.
preps.fix: Water 1000 to 1200 ml: Lebovitz's muscovado syrup is 50 g sugar to 60 ml water. Keep 504 to 168 h: he says at least a week, the only keep we can cite.

steps.body: Break up any lumps in the muscovado, then combine with the hot water.
Stir over low heat until fully dissolved.
Strain through a fine sieve to catch undissolved lumps, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: His muscovado syrup: 50 g dark brown sugar heated with 60 ml water (1 : 1.2). We use dark muscovado at the same ratio, scaled to 1 kg sugar.
Refrigerated, at least a week; we take the week.

preps.name: Oleo saccharum
preps.description: Lemon peels rested in an equal weight of sugar until their oils dissolve it into a fragrant syrup. The aromatic base of classic punch, and the first step of a sherbet.
preps.fix: Sugar 200 g to 100 g: both sources use equal weights of peel and sugar (was 1:2). Rest set to 8 to 12 h as the source gives. Keep 168 h to 336 h, the source's keep for this recipe.

recipe.note: from about 8 lemons, no white pith

steps.body: Peel the lemons with a vegetable peeler, taking as little white pith as possible.
Weigh the peels, add the same weight of sugar and muddle firmly to bruise them.
Cover (or vacuum seal) and rest at room temperature for 8 to 12 hours, until the sugar has turned into a wet, oily syrup. Stir once or twice.
Strain off the peels, pressing to collect all the syrup. If sugar is left on the peels, rinse them with a splash of warm water before straining.

sources.note: 1 part citrus peel to 1 part sugar by weight, muddled and rested 8 to 12 h at room temperature.
Up to two weeks in the fridge, for this 1:1 oleo.
Second source: roughly equal parts lemon peel and sugar, by weight.

preps.name: Olive oil-washed gin
preps.description: Gin shaken with extra virgin olive oil, frozen and strained. Gives Martinis a silky texture and a green, peppery olive note.
preps.fix: Olive oil up from 100 ml to 112 ml per 700 ml: Geoffrey Zakarian (Food Network) uses 4 oz (120 ml) per 750 ml gin, 12 hours at room temperature then 12 hours frozen. Added those times. Keep cut from 2160 h to 168 h: Drinks World gives 1 to 2 weeks for fat washes.

steps.body: Combine the gin and olive oil in a wide container, seal and shake hard.
Leave at room temperature for 12 hours.
Freeze for 12 hours, until the oil has set and separated.
Working quickly while it is still frozen, strain the gin through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter. Bottle, date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Geoffrey Zakarian: 4 oz (120 ml) extra virgin olive oil to a 750 ml bottle of dry gin (plus thyme, left out here), 12 hours at room temperature, 12 hours frozen, strained. Scaled to 700 ml: 112 ml.
General fat-washing guide: fat-washed spirits, kept in the fridge, last about 1 to 2 weeks. We take the shorter end (Zakarian says 6 months frozen).

preps.name: Orgeat
preps.description: Almond syrup: ground sweet almonds steeped in hot 1:1 syrup, strained, with a dash of brandy and orange flower water. Essential to the Mai Tai, Japanese Cocktail and Army and Navy.
preps.fix: Changed to the sourced method and ratio: ground almonds steeped 3 to 12 h in hot 1:1 syrup (230 g almonds, 300 g sugar, 300 g water, 30 g brandy, 1/4 tsp orange flower water), doubled. Was 300 g almonds to 600 ml water and 600 g sugar as almond milk, no alcohol. Added brandy (both sources list it; it helps the keep). Keep 336 h to 672 h, the source's keep for this recipe. Dropped alias 'orgeat works or small hand foods' (brand names, not a name for the prep).

recipe.note: sweet almonds only, blanched, slivered or whole

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Use sweet almonds only. Never add bitter almonds, apricot kernels or cherry pits: they can release cyanide.
Bring the water and sugar to the boil, stirring, then simmer gently until the sugar has dissolved.
Pulse the almonds in a blender or food processor until coarsely ground, stir them into the hot syrup and take off the heat.
Cover and steep for at least 3 hours and up to 12.
Strain through cheesecloth or a nut milk bag and discard the almonds. Stir in the brandy and orange flower water, bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

sources.note: 300 g sugar, 300 g water, 230 g blanched almonds steeped 3 to 12 h, then 30 g brandy or vodka and 1/4 tsp orange flower water (optional cherry pits left out). Doubled.
About a month in the fridge, for this recipe with brandy or vodka.
Second source gives the same cup amounts (2 cups almonds, 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/4 cups water) with optional brandy and a steep of 3 to 12 h.

preps.name: Pandan syrup
preps.description: Fresh pandan leaves blended with water, strained and made into syrup. Grassy, nutty and vanilla-like; common in Southeast Asian style drinks with rum and coconut.
preps.fix: Pandan 40 g to 85 g per 500 ml water and 500 g sugar (source: 100 g leaves, 600 ml water, 600 g sugar; water and sugar unchanged); method now blends the leaves with the water and strains the juice before adding sugar, as the source does, instead of simmering the leaves; keep 336 h to 168 h (shortest sourced keep, 1 week).

steps.body: Blend the chopped pandan leaves with the water until roughly broken down. Do not blend too long or it turns bitter.
Strain through a cloth, squeezing out the green juice. Discard the pulp.
Warm the juice with the sugar over a low heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and it thickens slightly.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

sources.note: 100 g chopped pandan leaves blended with 600 ml water, strained, then heated with 600 g white sugar. Scaled to 500 ml water: 85 g pandan, 500 g sugar.
Keep for this same recipe: fridge, up to two weeks, best within a week.
Keep for a less sweet blended pandan syrup (half a cup each of water and sugar): fridge, up to a week. Shorter keep, so we use it.

preps.name: Passion fruit syrup
preps.description: Unsweetened passion fruit purée whisked with an equal volume of rich syrup. Tart and tropical; used in the Hurricane, Porn Star Martini and tiki drinks.
preps.fix: Lines changed from sugar and water (about 565 ml rich syrup to 500 ml purée) to 500 ml rich simple syrup to 500 ml purée, the sourced 1:1 by volume. Keep cut from 336 h to 240 h (source: 10 days).

steps.body: Whisk the purée and cooled rich syrup together in a bowl until even.
Bottle, seal and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

sources.note: Smuggler's Cove style: 1.5 cups passion fruit purée to 1.5 cups cooled 2:1 syrup, whisked. Scaled to 500 ml each.
Second source runs 1:1 simple syrup to purée (a 1:1 syrup, not 2:1). We use the rich Smuggler's Cove version, which matches the current recipe and dilutes drinks less.
Keep for this same recipe (purée with equal 2:1 syrup): 10 days.

preps.name: Peach syrup
preps.description: Ripe peaches simmered in sugar syrup and strained. Used in Bellini style drinks, iced tea, bourbon smashes and sodas.
preps.fix: Peach 500 g to 2 large peaches, sugar 500 g to 300 g, water 500 ml to 480 ml (source: 2 cups water, 1.5 cups sugar, 2 large peaches); simmer time added (15 minutes); yield 1000 ml to 600 ml (sourced); keep 336 h to 168 h (shortest sourced keep, 1 week).

recipe.note: large and ripe, stoned and sliced, skin on (about 2 cups)

steps.body: Put the water, sugar and sliced peaches in a pan and bring to the boil.
Turn down and simmer until the peaches are soft and the liquid is syrupy.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit to get all the juice.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge. It thickens as it chills.

sources.note: Doubled batch as given: 2 cups water, 1.5 cups sugar, 2 large peaches (about 2 cups sliced), simmered 15 minutes. Cups converted: 480 ml water, 300 g sugar.
About 1.25 cups per single batch; doubled, about 2.5 cups (600 ml).
Keep for this same recipe: airtight in the fridge, about a month.
Keep for a less sweet peach syrup (1 cup peaches, 1 cup water, half a cup sugar): fridge, up to a week. Shorter keep, so we use it.

preps.name: Pineapple shrub
preps.description: Fresh pineapple macerated with sugar, strained and mixed with cider vinegar. Tangy and tropical; pairs with rum, tequila and soda.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged

recipe.note: ripe, peeled and cut into small chunks

steps.body: Toss the pineapple with the sugar, cover and rest in the fridge until the sugar has drawn out a thick syrup, about a day.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit and scraping in any undissolved sugar.
Add the vinegar and stir or shake until all the sugar has dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Throw it out if it turns bubbly, cloudy, slimy or mouldy.

sources.note: UC Master Food Preservers give equal parts fruit, sugar and vinegar (1:1:1) as the common shrub formula, with apple cider vinegar as the all-purpose choice. 500 g of each.
General shrub storage advice for the same cold-process shrubs: refrigerated, up to a year. We keep our shorter 8 weeks.

preps.name: Pineapple syrup
preps.description: Fresh pineapple macerated overnight in sugar, then loosened with water and strained. A classic 19th century syrup used in the Pisco Punch and East India Cocktail.
preps.fix: Water cut from 500 ml to 300 ml to match the sourced 500 g pineapple : 500 g sugar : 300 ml water. Method now macerates the fruit in sugar overnight before adding water. Keep 336 h unchanged (source allows 3 months).

recipe.note: ripe, peeled and cut into pieces

steps.body: Toss the pineapple pieces with the sugar in an airtight container and leave in the fridge overnight.
Add the water and stir until the sugar has dissolved.
Strain through a damp cloth and discard the fruit.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Breville Test Kitchen: 250 g peeled pineapple, 250 g caster sugar, 150 ml water; macerated overnight, then water added. Scaled x2.
Keep for this same recipe: up to 3 months in the fridge. We keep the shorter 2 weeks already in use for a fresh fruit syrup.

preps.name: Pineapple-infused rum
preps.description: Rum infused with fresh pineapple for up to a day and strained. A house take on pineapple rum for daiquiris, Old Fashioneds and tiki drinks.
preps.fix: Changed from 400 g pineapple per 700 ml for 3 to 5 days to half a pineapple per 750 ml rum for 4 to 24 hours (BlackTail via Imbibe). Keep cut from 2160 h to 336 h: BlackTail says use within 2 weeks.

recipe.note: or white rum, as BlackTail uses, for a lighter style
ripe, peeled, cored and cut into small chunks

steps.body: Combine the pineapple and rum in a clean jar and seal.
Leave for 4 to 24 hours, depending on how strong you want it. Taste from 4 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve, then a coffee filter, pressing the fruit lightly.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Use within 2 weeks.

sources.note: BlackTail (Jesse Vida) via Imbibe: half a pineapple, peeled, cored and chopped, to a 750 ml bottle of white rum, soaked 4 to 24 hours, then strained.
Keep belongs to this same BlackTail standard infusion (pineapple in rum, strained).

preps.name: Piña Colada mix
preps.description: Pineapple juice, cream of coconut and fresh lime juice, ready to blend with rum and crushed ice. Use about 115 ml of mix per 60 ml of rum.
preps.fix: Rescaled to Difford's Piña Colada (2 2/3 pineapple : 2/3 cream of coconut : 1/2 lime) per 900 ml pineapple: cream of coconut 450 to 225 ml, lime 75 to 170 ml, salt dropped; serve changed to about 115 ml mix per 60 ml rum. Keep unchanged.

recipe.note: sweetened, such as Coco López, stirred well

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Warm the tin of cream of coconut in hot water and stir until smooth.
Blend all the ingredients briefly, without ice, until fully combined.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake hard before each use as the coconut fat separates.
To serve, blend about 115 ml of mix with 60 ml rum, then add crushed ice and blend again.

sources.note: Per drink: 2 oz rum, 2 2/3 oz pineapple juice, 1/2 oz lime juice, 2/3 oz cream of coconut, dry blended then blended with crushed ice. Non-rum parts scaled to 900 ml pineapple juice.
Keep given for a piña colada base of one can of Coco López to 48 oz pineapple juice (about the same sugar as ours, and no lime, so no more preserved). Up to five days; we keep 3.

preps.name: Raspberry cordial
preps.description: Raspberries steeped overnight in hot sugar water, strained clear and sharpened with citric acid. A tart red cordial for spritzes, gin drinks and sodas, or 1 part to 4 of water.
preps.fix: Replaced with SBS Food's ratio: raspberries 500 to 300 g, sugar 400 to 500 g, water 400 to 1000 ml (boiling), citric acid 10 g to 4 tsp (the source's 1 Australian tablespoon, 20 ml). Method is now an overnight steep in boiling water, not crushing with sugar. Yield 900 to 1300 ml (sourced). The source's elderflower cordial and bay leaf are left out. Keep 336 h unchanged (source: 2 weeks).

steps.body: Put the raspberries and sugar in a large heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water and stir until the sugar has dissolved.
Cover and leave to steep overnight.
Strain through a fine sieve and let it drip through on its own. Do not press the pulp, or the cordial turns cloudy.
Whisk the citric acid into the strained syrup, pour into sterilised bottles and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 300 g raspberries, 500 g caster sugar, 1 L boiling water, 1 tbsp citric acid (Australian tablespoon, 20 ml, so 4 tsp); steep overnight, strain without pressing, whisk in the acid. Elderflower cordial and bay leaf left out.
Makes about 1.3 litres.
Keep for this same SBS recipe: up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Raspberry shrub
preps.description: Raspberries macerated with sugar, strained and mixed with cider vinegar. A sweet and sour drinking vinegar for highballs, spritzes and non-alcoholic serves.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged

steps.body: Crush the raspberries with the sugar, cover and rest in the fridge until the sugar has drawn out a thick syrup, about a day.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit and scraping in any undissolved sugar.
Add the vinegar and stir or shake until all the sugar has dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. The flavour mellows and improves after a few days. Throw it out if it turns bubbly, cloudy, slimy or mouldy.

sources.note: UC Master Food Preservers give equal parts fruit, sugar and vinegar (1:1:1) as the common shrub formula, macerating fruit with sugar about 24 hours before adding vinegar. 500 g of each.
General shrub storage advice for the same cold-process 1:1:1 shrubs: refrigerated, up to a year. We keep our shorter 8 weeks.

preps.name: Raspberry syrup
preps.description: Crushed raspberries macerated in sugar, then loosened with warm water and strained into a bright red syrup. Called for in the Clover Club and many classic punches and fizzes.
preps.fix: Was 500 g raspberries, 500 g sugar, 500 ml hot water (unsourced 1:1:1). Both sources run about 1 berry : 2 sugar : 1 water by volume, so now 150 g raspberries, 500 g sugar, 300 ml warm water, with a 30 minute maceration. Keep 336 h unchanged (Imbibe: 2 weeks).

steps.body: Crush the raspberries and mix them well with the sugar. Leave to macerate.
Warm the water (warm, not hot), pour it over the fruit and stir until all the sugar has dissolved.
Strain through a fine sieve or chinois. Let it drip rather than pressing hard, which clouds the syrup.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Julie Reiner: 1/2 cup raspberries, 1 cup sugar, 1/2 cup water, macerated 30 min. Converted (raspberries about 123 g a cup per USDA tables, sugar 200 g, water 120 ml) and scaled x2.5. Reiner adds 15 ml vodka to fortify; we leave it out, as Imbibe does.
Second source: 2 cups demerara sugar, 1 cup water, 1 cup raspberries, the same 1 : 2 : 1 proportions by volume as Reiner. Agrees.
Keep for Imbibe's raspberry syrup, same sugar level as ours and no spirit: up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Rhubarb syrup
preps.description: Chopped rhubarb simmered with sugar, water and a little vanilla, left to infuse for a day, then strained to a pink, tart syrup. Used in spritzes, gin sours and sodas.
preps.fix: Batch changed to the source's 400 g rhubarb, 400 g sugar, 600 ml water and 1 tsp vanilla extract (was 500 : 500 : 500 with no vanilla, so water is now 1.5 times the rhubarb); method now simmers 5 minutes and infuses about 24 hours before straining, as the source does; yield 950 ml to 900 ml (derived); keep 336 h unchanged (cited).

steps.body: Trim away all the leaves (they are not edible) and chop the stalks.
Bring the rhubarb, sugar, water and vanilla to the boil, then simmer.
Take off the heat, cover and leave to infuse.
Strain through a fine sieve, bring the syrup briefly back to the boil, then bottle, cool and keep in the fridge.
