sources.note: Lurch: 400 g rhubarb, 400 g sugar, 600 ml water, 1 tsp vanilla extract; boil, simmer 5 minutes, infuse about 24 hours, strain, reboil, bottle. Source batch as written.
Keep for a less sweet rhubarb syrup (454 g rhubarb, 480 ml water, 200 g sugar): fridge, up to two weeks.

preps.name: Rich demerara syrup
preps.description: Two parts demerara sugar to one part water by weight. The usual sweetener for an Old Fashioned and other stirred drinks, measured by the barspoon.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged; keep removed: no source

steps.body: Combine the demerara sugar and water in a pan over low heat.
Stir until completely dissolved, without letting it boil.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Demerara syrup is most often two parts sugar to one part water. Scaled to 1 kg sugar.
Its demerara syrup is 200 g demerara to 100 g water (2:1 by weight), plus optional extras we leave out.

preps.name: Rich honey syrup
preps.description: Three parts honey to one part water by weight. Thicker and less diluting than 2:1 honey syrup, but it still pours and dissolves in cold drinks.
preps.fix: Honey 1000 to 1500 g (3:1 by weight, from Difford's): at 2:1 it was the same as our Honey syrup and only about 55% sugar, not rich. Added description, steps, storage and the Syrup tag. 2:1 aliases moved to Honey syrup. No keep: no source.

steps.body: Weigh the honey into a container and add the warm water.
Stir until fully blended and smooth; it takes longer than a thinner syrup. Do not boil.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Honey syrup at 3 parts honey to 1 part water by weight. Scaled to 1.5 kg honey.

preps.name: Rich simple syrup
preps.description: Two parts white sugar to one part water by weight. Sweeter and thicker than 1:1 syrup, so it adds less dilution and keeps longer.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged

steps.body: Combine the sugar and water in a pan over low heat.
Stir until every crystal has dissolved and the syrup is clear. Take it off the heat before it simmers.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Two parts sugar to one part water, by weight in its example (2 kg sugar to 1 kg water). Scaled to 1 kg sugar.
Rich simple is two parts white sugar to one part water, about 66.6 Brix. Agrees with Difford's.
Side by side fridge test: 2:1 syrup lasted six months before clouding. We keep 8 weeks, well inside that.

preps.name: Saline solution
preps.description: Twenty percent salt dissolved in water by weight. A drop or two seasons a drink, taming bitterness and lifting citrus and sweetness without tasting salty.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (20% by weight). Keep lowered from 4320 to 4032 h (source: up to 6 months, at 4 weeks a month), and storage changed from room temperature to the fridge, which is what that keep is for. Added a description.

recipe.note: fine sea salt or kosher salt, not iodised

steps.body: Weigh the salt and the warm water.
Stir or shake until the salt has completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Decant into a dropper or dasher bottle, label with the strength and date, and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 20% saline: 80 g water to 20 g kosher salt (non-iodised), stirred to dissolve; tested by the drop in cocktails. Scaled to 1 kg.
20 g sea salt to 80 ml warm water, stirred clear, then into a dropper or spray bottle.
Keep for Drinksworld's own 80 g water to 20 g salt saline, the same strength as ours: up to 6 months (6 x 4 weeks) in a sealed dropper bottle in the fridge.

preps.name: Saline solution (10%)
preps.description: Ten percent salt dissolved in water by weight. A gentler saline that is easier to dose by the dash in batches and single drinks.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (the cited 10:1 water to salt is about 9%; ours is 10% by weight, within 10%). Keep removed: no source.

recipe.note: fine sea salt or kosher salt, not iodised

steps.body: Weigh the salt and the warm water.
Stir or shake until the salt has completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Decant into a dropper or dasher bottle and label with the strength and date.

sources.note: Little Red Door's low strength saline: distilled water to kosher salt 10:1 by weight, dashed into most drinks.

preps.name: Sangrita
preps.description: A tequila chaser of tomato, orange and lime juice with hot sauce, salt and pepper, given heat by a short jalapeño steep. Served chilled alongside the spirit.
preps.fix: Rewritten to Feast and West's 3:2:1 tomato, orange and lime (was 4:2:1), scaled to 1.2 litres; grenadine dropped (not in the source), hot sauce 20 ml to 5 dashes, salt 4 g to 3 pinches, adds black pepper and a short jalapeño steep as the source does. keep removed: no source

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Juice and fine strain the orange and lime.
Stir the tomato, orange and lime juices together with the hot sauce, salt and pepper.
Drop in the halved jalapeños and leave for 15 to 30 minutes, tasting as you go, then lift them out.
Bottle, chill well and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 6 oz tomato, 4 oz orange and 2 oz lime juice (3:2:1) with 1 to 2 dashes hot sauce, a pinch each of salt and pepper and one halved jalapeño steeped 15 to 30 minutes. Scaled x 3.3 to 1.2 litres.

preps.name: Simple syrup
preps.description: Equal parts white sugar and water by weight. The standard bar sweetener for sours, highballs and most shaken drinks.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged

steps.body: Weigh the sugar and the water into a clean container. Use equal weights.
Stir or blend until the sugar has fully dissolved and the syrup is clear. Hot water speeds this up; do not boil or the ratio will drift.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: One part sugar to one part water (1:1); Difford's notes weighing gives a slightly sweeter syrup than measuring by volume. Scaled to 1 kg sugar.
Simple is equal parts white sugar and water by weight, about 50 Brix. Agrees with Difford's.
Side by side fridge test: plain 1:1 syrup lasted a month before clouding. We keep 3 weeks, inside that.

preps.name: Sour mix
preps.description: Equal fresh lemon and lime juice mixed with one and a half parts simple syrup. A ready sweet and sour base for high volume sours, margaritas and collinses.
preps.fix: Lemon juice 500 to 250 ml so lemon and lime are equal, as in VinePair; simple syrup kept at 750 ml, which now runs 1.5 parts to 1 part juice (VinePair's 1 cup sugar in 1 cup water to 1 cup juice). Keep unchanged.

steps.body: Juice and fine strain the lemons and limes.
Combine the juices with the cooled simple syrup and shake or stir.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Best used within a day.

sources.note: 1 cup sugar boiled into 1 cup water, cooled, then mixed with 1/2 cup each lime and lemon juice. That syrup is about 1.5 cups, so 1.5 parts syrup to 1 part juice; scaled to 500 ml juice.
Keep given for this same VinePair recipe: about a week covered in the fridge. We keep our shorter 2 days for flavour.

preps.name: Spiced syrup
preps.description: Simple syrup simmered with cinnamon, clove and star anise and a little honey. A warm baking spice note for winter drinks, punches and Old Fashioneds.
preps.fix: Sugar 500 g to 415 g, cinnamon 10 g to 2 sticks, cloves 3 g to 4 whole, star anise 3 to 2, honey 30 ml added, orange peel removed (the sourced recipe has none) (source: 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar, 1 tbsp honey, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 star anise, 2 cloves); yield 780 ml to 750 ml (sourced); keep 504 h unchanged (below the sourced two months).

steps.body: Put everything in a pan and bring to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Turn the heat to low and simmer.
Take off the heat and leave the spices in as it cools to room temperature.
Strain through a fine sieve, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 1 cup water, 1 cup cane sugar, 1 tbsp honey, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 star anise, 2 cloves; simmer 5 minutes, cool, strain. Cups converted (240 ml, 200 g) and scaled to 500 ml water: 415 g sugar, 30 ml honey, 2 sticks, 2 star anise, 4 cloves.
About 1.5 cups (360 ml) per cup of water; scaled to 500 ml water, about 750 ml.
Keep for this same recipe: airtight in the fridge, up to two months. We keep the shorter three weeks already set.

preps.name: Strawberry shrub
preps.description: Strawberries macerated with sugar, strained and mixed with white wine vinegar. Bright and jammy with a sharp finish; good with gin, tequila and soda.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged

steps.body: Toss the strawberries with the sugar, cover and rest in the fridge until the sugar has drawn out a thick syrup, about a day.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit and scraping in any undissolved sugar.
Add the vinegar and stir or shake until all the sugar has dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Throw it out if it turns bubbly, cloudy, slimy or mouldy.

sources.note: UC Master Food Preservers give equal parts fruit, sugar and vinegar (1:1:1) as the common shrub formula, and suggest white wine vinegar for delicately flavoured fruit. 500 g of each.
General shrub storage advice for the same cold-process shrubs: refrigerated, up to a year. We keep our shorter 8 weeks.

preps.name: Strawberry syrup
preps.description: Quartered strawberries steeped in hot simple syrup for hours, then strained into a red fruit syrup. Used in daiquiris, spritzes and sodas.
preps.fix: Was 500 g strawberries, 500 g sugar, 500 ml water; the source converts to about 380 g berries and 600 ml water per 500 g sugar, steeped 6 hours in hot syrup. Keep cut from 336 h to 168 h (Imbibe: 1 week).

steps.body: Put the quartered strawberries in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the sugar and water, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved.
Pour the hot syrup over the strawberries and leave to steep, stirring now and then.
Strain into a clean bottle without pressing hard, and keep in the fridge. The berries can be used as garnish.

sources.note: Joy Richard: 1 cup quartered strawberries, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water; hot syrup poured over, 6 hours. Converted (strawberries about 152 g a cup per USDA tables, sugar 200 g, water 240 ml) and scaled x2.5.
Keep for this same recipe: up to 1 week in the fridge.

preps.name: Strawberry-infused Campari
preps.description: Campari infused with fresh strawberries for a day or two. Softens the bitterness and adds ripe berry flavour to Negronis and spritzes.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged (StarChefs: 16 oz strawberries per litre of Campari, at least 24 hours; ours is within 10%). Keep removed: no source.

steps.body: Combine the sliced strawberries and Campari in a clean jar and seal.
Infuse in the fridge for at least 24 hours and up to 48, shaking once or twice.
Strain through a fine sieve, then a coffee filter, without pressing the fruit.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: StarChefs: 16 oz (454 g) halved strawberries to 1 litre Campari, at least 24 hours. Scaled to 700 ml that is 318 g; our 350 g is within 10%.

preps.name: Super lemon juice
preps.description: Lemon peel oils pulled out with citric acid, blended with water and topped with the fruit's juice. A longer lasting, low waste stand-in for fresh lemon juice.
preps.fix: Cited; peel, acid and water amounts unchanged. Lemon juice amount removed: sources add all the juice of the peeled lemons unmeasured, and none gives a volume. Keep 120 h unchanged (sources give 1 week). Added a 1 hour rest timer from the source.

recipe.note: from about 6 lemons, no white pith
all the juice of the peeled lemons

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Weigh the lemon peels. Everything scales from them: 1 g citric acid and 16.6 ml water per gram of peel.
Toss the peels with the citric acid in a covered container and leave, shaking now and then, until an oily slurry has formed.
Add the water and blend with a stick blender until the peels are finely chopped.
Strain through a fine cloth or superbag, squeezing it out.
Juice the peeled lemons, add all the juice, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: For lemon, citric acid equal to the peel weight and no malic; water at 16.66 x peel weight; juice of the peeled fruit added unmeasured.
Same lemon ratio: citric acid equal to the peel weight, water at 16.66 x peel weight.
Keep for Hilda's own lemon recipe (same ratios): blending the peels, as we do, cuts it to 1 week.
Keep for Pinestraw's own recipes (same lemon ratio): all at their best for the first week, turning metallic and bitter after.

preps.name: Super lime juice
preps.description: Lime peel oils pulled out with citric and malic acid, blended with water and topped with the fruit's juice. Nickle Morris's method for stretching a few limes into a lime juice stand-in.
preps.fix: Cited; amounts unchanged. Keep 120 h unchanged (sources give 1 week once blended). Added a 1 hour rest timer from the source.

recipe.note: from about 8 limes, no white pith

keeps.storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Weigh the lime peels. Everything scales from them: 0.66 g citric acid, 0.33 g malic acid and 16.6 ml water per gram of peel.
Toss the peels with both acids in a covered container and leave, shaking now and then, until an oily slurry has formed.
Add the water and blend with a stick blender until the peels are finely chopped.
Strain through a fine cloth or superbag, squeezing it out.
Juice the peeled limes, add the juice, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Credits Nickle Morris. For lime, peel weight x 0.66 citric acid and x 0.33 malic acid, then water at 16.66 x peel weight; acids rest on the peels 1 to 2 hours; juice of the peeled fruit added. Matches ours per 100 g peel.
Credits Nickle Morris. Acids equal to the peel weight, two parts citric to one malic; about 8 limes for roughly a litre. Agrees with our acid amounts.
Eight limes give about 100 g of peel and almost 8 oz (about 240 ml) of juice, which supports our 250 ml. Its lime acid ratio (0.4 citric, 0.3 malic) differs; we use the 0.66 and 0.33 above.
Keep for Hilda's own recipe (same 0.66/0.33/16.66 ratios): a month unblended, but blending the peels, as we do, cuts it to 1 week.
Keep for VinePair's 8 lime recipe (44 g citric, 8 g malic, 4 cups water), less acid than ours: one to two weeks refrigerated; we take the shorter end.

preps.name: Tea-infused vermouth
preps.description: Sweet vermouth infused with loose black tea for about 90 minutes. Adds tannin and a dry, spiced note to Manhattans, Negronis and punches.
preps.fix: Changed from 8 g black tea per 700 ml for 20 minutes to 3 tbsp loose tea per 750 ml for about 90 minutes: Death & Co's tea-infused vermouth (Mother's Ruin Punch) uses 1 heaping tbsp per 250 ml. Keep 672 h now cited (VinePair: opened vermouth about a month, refrigerated).

recipe.note: loose leaf, heaping; Death & Co use a cinnamon-orange black tea

steps.body: Stir the loose tea into the vermouth in a clean jar.
Leave at room temperature for about 90 minutes, stirring now and then.
Strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve, then a coffee filter, without squeezing the leaves.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge like any opened vermouth.

sources.note: Death & Co: 1 heaping tbsp (or 3 bags) cinnamon-orange tea to 250 ml sweet vermouth, about 90 minutes at room temperature, strained through cheesecloth. Scaled to 750 ml: 3 tbsp.
Keep belongs to plain opened vermouth, refrigerated. Steeping tea adds no sugar or alcohol, so the infused vermouth is no more preserved than plain.

preps.name: Tepache
preps.description: A Mexican drink of pineapple fermented for two to three days with piloncillo, tamarind and spices. Lightly fizzy, tangy and sweet.
preps.fix: Rewritten to America's Test Kitchen's ratio, halved to 2 litres of water: pineapple 600 g rind to 825 g cored fruit with rind, piloncillo 250 to 350 g, cinnamon 5 to 20 g, cloves 3 each to 3/8 tsp; adds tamarind, morita chile and coriander seed as ATK does; ferment at 22 to 23 C stirring daily. Keep unchanged.

recipe.note: broken into chunks, or dark brown sugar
rinsed, trimmed, quartered and cored, rind on

keeps.storage: Fridge, bottle with lid loose to vent gas

steps.body: Put the piloncillo, tamarind, cinnamon, chile, coriander and cloves in a large clean glass jar. Add half the water, then the pineapple, then the rest of the water.
Cover with cheesecloth and leave somewhere dark, ideally 22 to 23 C. Stir once a day with a clean spoon so no fruit or spice sits dry on top.
Start tasting after 2 days; it usually takes 2 to 3. Throw it away if it grows fuzzy mould or smells unpleasant.
Strain out the solids, bottle and refrigerate. For more fizz, use pressure-safe bottles and leave them at room temperature 12 to 24 hours before chilling; vent daily after that.

sources.note: 700 g piloncillo, 50 g tamarind, 40 g Mexican cinnamon, 1 morita chile, 1 tbsp coriander seed, 3/4 tsp cloves, 4,000 g water and 1,650 g cored pineapple, fermented 2 to 3 days at 72 to 74 F. Halved.
1 gallon (3,785 ml) from 4,000 g water; halved to about 1,890 ml.
Keep given for this same ATK tepache: up to a week in the fridge.

preps.name: Thyme syrup
preps.description: Simple syrup simmered with fresh thyme sprigs. Gently herbal and earthy; works with gin, lemon, honey and stone fruit.
preps.fix: Water raised from 500 ml to 600 ml and thyme changed from 20 g to 20 sprigs, to match the source (4 sprigs per 1/2 cup each sugar and water, scaled to 500 g sugar). Thyme now cools in the syrup. Keep cut from 504 h to 336 h (Imbibe: 2 weeks).

steps.body: Put the water, sugar and thyme in a pan over medium heat.
Bring to a simmer, stirring often, until the sugar has dissolved.
Leave to cool to room temperature with the thyme in.
Strain into a clean bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Julie Wallach: 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup water, 4 thyme sprigs, simmered and cooled with the herb in. Converted (cup sugar 200 g, cup water 240 ml) and scaled x5.
Keep for this same recipe: up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Tom and Jerry batter
preps.description: A thick, spiced batter of beaten yolks and rum folded into stiff egg whites and thickened with sugar. Spooned into a mug with rum and brandy and topped with hot milk.
preps.fix: Cited (Imbibe, Oakland Art Novelty Co.): eggs, sugar and rum unchanged; rum is Jamaican as sourced; spices changed to the source's 1.5 tsp clove, 1.5 tsp allspice, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 tsp anise, with vanilla and nutmeg dropped; method now folds yolks into whites, then sugar, as the source does. Yield removed: eggs are counted by number, so a weight can't be checked. Keep unchanged.

steps.body: Separate the eggs. Whisk the yolks until even, then drizzle in the rum while whisking.
In a large clean bowl, whisk the whites to stiff peaks.
Fold the yolk mixture into the whites a third at a time, adding the spices as you fold.
Fold in the sugar a little at a time until the batter is thick and even.
Contains raw egg: keep chilled, use the same day and tell guests. To serve, spoon batter into a warm mug, add rum and brandy and top with hot milk while stirring.

sources.note: 12 eggs, 1 oz Jamaican rum, 1 1/2 tsp each ground cloves and allspice, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground anise, 2 lb cane sugar; yolks and rum folded into stiff whites, then sugar. 2 lb at 450 g per lb.

Ohio State Extension storage chart, general keep for raw egg whites (2 to 4 days refrigerated; raw yolks 1 week). The batter is raw egg plus sugar; we keep it one day, and the recipe says use it straight away.

preps.name: Vanilla syrup
preps.description: Simple syrup steeped with split vanilla pods, seeds left in. Used in tiki drinks, the Porn Star Martini and coffee cocktails.
preps.fix: Water was 1 litre to 1 kg sugar with 2 pods; the source runs more water (1 cup to each cup of sugar, about 1.2 : 1 by weight) and 1 pod per 400 g sugar, so now 960 ml water, 800 g sugar, 2 pods. Steep is 1 hour after a simmer. Keep 504 h unchanged (source allows 1 month).

recipe.note: pods, split lengthways and seeds scraped

steps.body: Put the sugar, water, scraped seeds and split pods in a pan.
Bring to a simmer, stirring until the sugar has dissolved.
Turn off the heat, cover and steep.
Lift out the pods (the seeds can stay), cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 2 cups water, 2 cups sugar, 1 split vanilla bean, simmered then steeped covered for 1 hour. Converted (1 cup water 240 ml, 1 cup sugar 200 g) and doubled: 960 ml water, 800 g sugar, 2 pods.
Keep for this same recipe: 1 month refrigerated. We keep the shorter 3 weeks already in use.

preps.name: Vanilla tincture
preps.description: Split vanilla pods steeped in strong vodka for at least six weeks. A few dashes add vanilla aroma without the sweetness of a syrup or liqueur.
preps.fix: Vanilla pods up from 6 to 8 per 250 ml: ATK steeps 8 beans in 1 cup (240 ml) vodka. Steep time changed from about 14 days to at least 6 weeks, as ATK gives. Vodka now 50% ABV so the ATK bitters keep applies. Keep 8760 h confirmed.

keeps.storage: Room temperature, dropper bottle, away from light

steps.body: Split the vanilla pods lengthways, chop them and put them in a clean jar with the vodka.
Seal and keep somewhere dark for at least 6 weeks (up to 10), giving it a gentle shake once a week.
Strain through a sieve lined with two coffee filters into dropper bottles and label.

sources.note: ATK vanilla extract: 8 vanilla beans (1 oz) to 1 cup (240 ml) vodka, 6 to 10 weeks in the dark, strained through coffee filters. Scaled to 250 ml (8.3 pods, rounded to 8).

Keep belongs to ATK aromatic bitters: botanicals in 100-proof vodka plus a little simple syrup. Ours is unsweetened at 50% ABV, so at least as preserved. ATK's vanilla extract page says it keeps indefinitely.

preps.name: Vanilla-infused vodka
preps.description: Vodka infused with a split vanilla pod for several days. A house vanilla vodka for Porn Star Martinis and Espresso Martinis.
preps.fix: Vanilla cut from 2 pods to 1 per 700 ml and time from 3 to 5 days to 3 to 6 days: Difford's uses one quality pod per bottle (we read it as 70 cl). A second source runs stronger (3 beans per 750 ml, 5 to 7 days). Keep removed: no source.

recipe.note: good pod, about 15 cm, split lengthways

steps.body: Split the vanilla pod lengthways and drop it into the vodka.
Seal and infuse at room temperature for 3 to 6 days, shaking whenever you pass it.
Strain through a fine sieve or coffee filter once the flavour is full, then bottle and label as vanilla-infused.

sources.note: Difford's: one quality vanilla pod (about 15 cm), split, in a freshly opened bottle of vodka for 3 to 6 days, then filtered. We read the bottle as 70 cl.
Second source runs stronger: 3 vanilla beans to 750 ml vodka, 5 to 7 days shaking daily. We use Difford's lighter ratio.
